Right: the new graph keeps just those four nodes and the three edges among them, A–B, B–C, and B–E; nodes D and F and every edge touching them are dropped, shown dashed." width="100%"} Extracts the currently selected nodes or edges into a new Graph object. The behavior depends on what's selected: - nodes selected: include those nodes plus all edges between them - edges selected: include those edges plus their endpoint nodes Nodes and edges keep their IDs, labels, weights and attributes, so results can be matched back to the original graph by ID. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : New Graph object containing the subgraph, with the same directedness and weighting as the original graph. Empty if nothing is selected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Extract a node-induced subgraph: ::: {#885086bc .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_path_graph(n=6) # Get node IDs for nodes at positions 2, 3, 4 all_node_ids = list(graph.get_node_ids(limit=None)) node_ids_to_select = [all_node_ids[2], all_node_ids[3], all_node_ids[4]] graph.select_nodes_by_id(node_ids=node_ids_to_select) subgraph = graph.transform_to_subgraph_ws() # Returns 3 subgraph.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#51a11c7f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 2 (edges between selected nodes) subgraph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Extract an edge-induced subgraph instead by selecting edges rather than nodes: ::: {#379f5413 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(5) edges = graph.get_edge_ids()[:2] graph.select_edges_by_id(edges) subgraph = graph.transform_to_subgraph_ws() subgraph.count_nodes(), subgraph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (3, 2) ``` ::: :::
